# Pre-freeze advice for Study B

**Verdict: do not freeze yet.** Three hypotheses need fixing first, and two of the planned measurements are already decided by short arguments. All of this is derived by hand here and nothing was run.

## Loopholes in the hypotheses

1. **"No implied rules" decides the answer by itself.**
   - Under the strong reading (the only minimal forbidden partial words of the allowed set are the monochromatic words on holders), the holders are read off the allowed words, so uniqueness is a tautology.
   - The six-distinction case fails that reading: the four "incident" triples imply the four "avoiding" triples and conversely. The search through nine therefore used a weaker reading.
   - Freeze one of: (a) the strong reading, (b) no implied rule on fewer than three distinctions, (c) no holder implied by the others. Report under each.
2. **The class of the second presentation is unstated.**
   - Without the same degree, arity and full-projection conditions on it, the union of the two six-distinction families is a trivial third presentation.
   - "Second" should mean a different named family of holders. The two six-distinction families are isomorphic as families, so "non-isomorphic" would wrongly exclude them.
3. **Connectedness must hold for both presentations.** It is what blocks the trivial counterexample of a closed six-distinction block beside a part with a loose distinction. Also state whether two holders may have identical supports.

## Loose-distinction reading

- **Structural:** the distinction lies in exactly one holder.
- **Semantic:** the words on the other distinctions at which it is forced form one partial word and its complement. A distinction in two holders gives a union of two such words.
- Preregister the semantic reading as the definition and test whether it coincides with the structural one on every census entry. It can fail only where an implied rule exists.
- "Flipping … leaves the allowed set" reads both as "exits" and "stays in". Write "the flipped word is allowed" or "is forbidden".

## Census method and attacks

- **Complete method:** compute the minimal sets of distinctions with no monochromatic allowed word. Every holder of any in-class presentation is one of them, by full projection. Then search the in-class subfamilies with the same allowed words.
- **Cheap attack:** compare the symmetries of the allowed words with those of the presentation. Any excess gives a second presentation. This is not complete, since a second family need not be an image of the first.
- **Likely proof route:** forgetting a loose distinction frees its whole holder, which is a parent step. A closed block cannot sit inside a connected larger presentation, so an induction may reduce the loose case to closed cores.

## Marginal bounds

- **Both upper bounds are lemmas, not census targets.** Words allowed on every p-projection satisfy every holder, so they are the allowed words. The same holds for zero monochromatic weight read at order 2⌊q/2⌋ for each arity q. Neither needs "no implied rules".
- **Odd orders carry nothing new.** Under a complement-symmetric weighting, order-r marginals for odd r are determined by order r−1. The eight-distinction pair agreeing on all pairs therefore agrees on all triples, so the planned triple test is vacuous. Test order 4.
- **Lower-bound witnesses must both be in-class, on the same distinctions.** They should agree through order 2⌊p/2⌋−2. A lone holder against the free cube or parity is not a witness.
- **The support-only lower bound is trivial.** Any two distinct in-class systems with no smaller implied rule agree on all (p−1)-projections.
- **Weighting:** name it (uniform on allowed words), use exact counts, and record it as a scaffold. A weighting that is not complement-symmetric loses the 2⌊p/2⌋ saving.
- **Holder marginals:** these are uniform on a holder's allowed words only when no chain of holders closes. Do not assume it with the extra meeting or on the five-holder chain.
- **Parity control:** run even and odd arity separately. Odd-arity even parity is not complement-closed, so it should need order p.

## Wording

- Use "distinction" throughout, not "mark" or "name"; "loose distinction"; "shared distinction" for "meeting".
- Replace "ten-width" with "ten distinctions".
- Say what grows in "exponentially growing".
- Say what a "start" is.
- "Tree" and "cycle" are the literature's words; give each once, marked as such.
